comment: Bathrooms are not available, the trail is little bit challenging but very beautiful..
Bring water and bug spray!!
Great trail! Well marked and good paths. Hills are solid, but not too challenging. Water and good shoes needed, lovely creeks and bridges throughout
Well blazed, pretty good views, pretty forests, lots of dogs to meet! Very few bugs at this time of year

Definitely among my top 3 trail recommendations for moderate difficulty but amazing flora and scenic views. We did all the side trails and ended up spending a good 4 hours here, covering almost 18kms. Absolutely in love with this trail, just a short drive away from Caledon. Highly recommend! Also, no bugs!!!
Humid and buggy

A serene, mostly forested trail—don't forget insect repellent, as the shaded woods attract plenty of bugs. The path features a number of charming wooden bridges crossing over gently flowing streams, each one inviting you to pause and take in the soothing sounds of water weaving through the landscape. Gentle inclines add a bit of challenge, making trekking poles a welcome companion, though they’re often rewarded with breezy, gradual descents. While much of the trail winds under a canopy of green, it occasionally opens into sunlit meadows sprinkled with wildflowers—a beautiful and refreshing contrast that feels like a reward in itself.
A lovely hike through varying terrain. Clean. Serene. Very well marked trail signs.Beautiful creeks. Totally refreshed….!
Fairly dry, a little overgrown in the Snell Lake Loop, and occasional bugs, but otherwise a fantastic quiet day in Hockley Valley!
Great trail for weight exercise
Beautiful little streams throughout, very hilly, bring lots of water
Moderate
Beautiful trail! Lots of up and down, glad I brought my hiking poles. Love the variety-woods, streams (great little bridges!), meadows. This is definitely a trail I’ll do again!
Beautiful

I have hiked this trail before and was wonderful surprise of the scenic views as if it was the first time seeing them.   Going across the wooden bridges and paused to look at the river it was just  breathtaking.  Overall I enjoy the hike...
Pretty river. No real places to sit for lunch.

It was a good day hike. We took our sweet time, otherwise this entire loop can be done in 4-6 hours. 

We didn’t not notice much wildlife. There were plenty of spots to sit, relax and chill. Few by the rivers and some near the ponds in open terrace like field.
It has multiple trial so you can choose Short distance or long distance. I want to hold trial together to come about three and a half hours.
Snow covered.
Beautiful scenery. Excellent trails. Great for group walks.
Beautiful trail. Arrive early to get your parking. Prepare to climb as the elevation is quite high. It was quiet as we arrived at 8:30 but got busier towards the end.
A lovely trail that actually has a little bit of up-and-down. Nice at this time of year with the changing leaves.
Lots of meandering creeks with a dozen or so bridges.
Bring walking poles. Or reuse discarded sticks at the entrance. Bring lots of water.
Hilly, a bit challenging
Beautiful trails very scenic, wooded area and also challenging hills. Definitely one must do.
Snell Lake loop section is very overgrown. Everywhere else is great! No mud, very few bugs, another great day at Hockley!

Pros: immaculate condition trail (it is the Bruce), some cool sights (like an abandoned old car), amazing workout and it's free with a large parking lot. 

Cons: there honestly isn't that much to see. No real lookouts or large bodies of water. There are a few places with those things nearby.

Great trail, perfect for an afternoon hike. We parked at the Hockley Valley Nature Reserve entrance, and it’s a short walk down the road from there to the trailhead. Lots of nice ups and downs, a winding stream you’ll keep coming back to, and some really well maintained forest trails that were surprisingly quiet on a Sunday afternoon. We got it done in 3 hours at a brisk walking pace.

Well blazed and well trod trail. Lovely forest and enough hills and crags to make you feel like it's a workout, not just a walk in the woods. On a quieter day might've rated this better.

Erosion is an issue in many places, no doubt because the trails are fairly crowded. Disappointed at how many folks were not respecting the trail, shouting, and blocking pathways.
Beautiful conditions, nice shade, very few bugs. A classic hike for May!
Free parking, the parking is not too crowded if you were there early. The trail conditions are very good. No bugs yet.
No bugs or mud. Ample parking at Hockey PNR. Well marked trails
Uphill

free parking https://maps.app.goo.gl/fZxm99yJQrhpQjjTA

Hilly, 12.6km, 5.5 hours
Beautiful section and the side trails make for a nice 14-15km from the parking lot.  Seems primarily rolling hardwood forests but the middle section with the bridges is beautiful.
It's a nice walk in the woods but not a whole lot to look at to make the trail stand out. Still glad I went
Beautiful day to be out on the trails. It was really icy in spots (absolutely needed spikes), not as muddy as I was expecting but generally it was a great hike
Very nice foresty trail, well maintained with the exception of a few fallen trees. Nothing exceptional but it’s was just a nice walk.
This trail was beautiful, with varying terrain. I think the distance for this exact trail may be a little longer than stated ~15 kms. Totally worth every step!
Parking lot was easy to find. Nice to do the longer 14km trail (not too challenging) but can also make it shorter if desired by skipping one of the loops or turning back.
Lots of up and downs.  No real lookouts. Super nice fall colours.
One of my favourite trails to hike.
Challenging with lots of ups and downs. Many mosquitoes to contend with. Pretty ridge walks and running water in the valleys.

your choice is either trail run the whole thing or spray generous amount of insect repellant all over your body. Like others have said, this is basically a hunting ground for local mosquitos at this time of the year.
No memorable scenery to speak of, just a regular forest hike with some little streams, foot bridges, that's all. Very moderate elevation changes, easy to do in three hours. 
Navigation can be confusing, be prepared.
Very nice work out. Weather is good and trail condition is very good as well.
Beautiful  easy/medium trail. Very well marked and not too rocky at all. A little bit of bugs. Big parking lot is a plus
Lots of mosquitoes!  Otherwise wonderful shady tree canopies offer respite on a hot sunny day.  Definitely a moderate level trail due to many ups and downs.
Beautiful trail but be prepared to be eaten alive by mosquitoes
Always an amazing and challenging hike. Bugs are out in full force so be prepared!
Great trail conditions, not muddy at all. The bugs are starting to come out, but not too pesky. Trilliums in bloom.
Interesting trail, not muddy, little to no bugs. Well marked.
Interesting landscape changes and a lot of fun

Little to no bugs, 90% covered under tree canopies so not much sun exposure which is good. 
Lots of ups and downs though. Hard on knees on the ways down. But still a great hike! Will be back!
Snow is cleared! The warm weather the last few days has evidently done wonders and cleared out all the remaining snow/ice except for one 50m patch that is easy to walk along (photo included)
A surprising amount of elevation for the region. Gorgeous valleys

Nice hike in the woods. Trail was in nice condition. Moderately challenging — some good slopes to push yourself on. Big parking lot, although it’s a popular trail so quite full. You can come back on a different loop that you walked out on, which is nice.

Got to the trail at about 9am, and there was a lot of parking - finished around 1pm and the lot was full. Trees were beautiful, trail was well marked and not too busy (especially in the morning). Had lunch about half way through by a really nice clearing near a pond. Lovely trail!
Beautiful trail on a sunny October day. It’s a lot of up and downs so tough on the knees. Great trail though

Beautiful and good work out for four plus hours.. .  Lots of ups and downs. Was expecting fall Colours.. at lower heights.. never mind green all around with fall colours at the sky level  was still a pretty sight . Will  definitely go back late fall  …
Overall very well marked, well maintained, no bikers allowed (thankfully). Good cardio, lots of ups and downs. Great trail.
Wonderful

￼￼Excellent trail and shout out to the man we met on the last trail who was a retired hiking guide and recommended this one for us. Epic climbs with hills and valleys, Rocky and lots of roots to navigate, beautiful trails end it definitely is one of our new favorites. Too bad we don’t live closer￼Perfect to piggyback it off of the 9 km we just finished. Solid day.￼
Great way to spend a beautiful Oct. 1st. Trail is well marked and not too much elevation.
Best hike within an hour of Toronto
Good.!!
Gorgeous and quiet. Bugs in some places (early July) but manageable. Great workout too — lots of ups and downs. The forests are spectacular.
Snapped a chain but aside from that it was great!
Dense, lush and engaging! A fantastic moderate workout and forest bath. Low crowd on a Sunday afternoon.
beautiful greenery, tall trees, low bugs, highly recommend.

Amazing section of the Bruce. What you're not going to get here are epic lookouts/vistas or waterfalls. What you will get is an amazing workout, lots of ups and downs, varied terrain and forest types and the "greatest hits" version of the Bruce Trail. Biting bugs are only out a little bit right now and the trail conditions are absolutely immaculate throughout.

Conditions are good, not very muddy at this time. Trees are starting to bud and greenery is peeking through - should be a lovely hike in a couple weeks. 

Lots of hills, but nothing too complicated. 
took 4.5 hrs to complete the entire loop + extension to Dunby Rd. (18 km total).

Nice trail with lots of great terrain and areas. Today was perfect weather, not muddy, no bugs yet but no flower nor foliage either. 2 weeks from now would see more flowers as I see lots of trees are putting out buds right now.
Soft but not muddy
Beautiful day. Perfect winter-early spring conditions. Lots of hills. Micro spikes are a must.
Trail was an excellent conditions great weather
Great conditions snow was perfect for hiking.   Creeks and valleys a pleasant place to hike.

Beautiful as always through the creaking trees.  

Lots of tree fall across the trails that you’ll have to climb over.
First snow fall of the year, gorgeous
This trail is amazing! First real snow of the season made it a winter wonderland. Very well marked. Slippery in areas so recommend spikes. Definitely want to come back in summer.
Lovely hike.  Lots of hills and not too muddy, even though it rained the day before.
pretty good considering proximity to Toronto. small detour from suggested route worth it if you like creeks.

Great terrain and elevation throughout.
We came across a porcupine on the main trail, which our dogs thankfully did not catch
Very nice trial for people not interested in very demanding hikes.
Awesome trail. Lots of hills! Do not be like me and do it the day after leg day…
Wonderful trail. Lots of up and down but nothing too tough.
One of my favorite trails. I go here a lot. So quiet and covered with tall & dense trees. Lots of ups and downs which make it a fun challenge.
Lovely changes in scenery, plenty of shade. We enjoyed this trail quite a bit.
Great. Well maintained. Lots of hills
Amazing trail. Very hilly.  Well maintained.  We did not see signage for some of the loops though
Quiet on the trails on a Saturday afternoon. Lots of room in the parking lot. Smooth, dirt trails the whole way (easy on ankles). Lots of up and down. Felt secluded at many times. A favorite.
lots of up and down, not a lot of bugs, great workout! a few benches and logs to have lunch
Awesome
Nice forest, lots of shade
Awesome. Quick 3 hours. No breaks. Good base training.

The trail is well marked, and lots of hills to keep an avid hiker entertained. Some great spots along the river you can take a nice break, and the bugs weren’t bad. Also not many people were out but that may have been because of the iffy weather.
A lot of inclines, but majority of the trail is in the shade, so it was nice on a hot sunny day. Bring plenty of water.
Trail is very nice. Too bad Uneducated people that garbage behind￼
Excellent Trail, except people leave their dog shit behind! M.F.

Very nice trail, covered by forest and not a lot of mosquitoes! 
But we finished with 15.1 km with full loops instead of 13.8 km listed in the summary.
Perfect workout and perfect beauty
Loved it!
Awesome
Very lush with tall trees and hills. Great for a somewhat rugged hike, not a stroll in the park. Well worth a visit!

Best trail I've experienced in the GTA so far - a real "hike for hikers ". From the initial ascent from the road, the hills do not let up - it almost feels like a hikers amusement park with three loops to challenge you. Beautifully maintained trails, bridges and related features - will definitely be back!

Great work out!!! Wonderful deep valleys of green, extremely large trees. Great hike. Only couple downsides... TONS of mosquitos even with spray ( to be expected) parking was a nightmare, and a lot of people; granted it was the long weekend. Overall very nice.
Great trail, a lot of up and down, however, it’s getting busier and busier...
Lovely, easy, though some steep up and down. Lots of other trail users including families, runners, and dogs.

Great ups and downs, stream, fields, forest, even wildlife. Saw a couple hawks, fox, toad, birds galore and beautiful patches of trillium in bloom (but not for long).  Great views and great workout, can't ask for more.
Great nature and shade for a good workout
It felt like a never-ending ups and downs, rarely flat. Good workout. Will return but probably not do all 3 loops in one day.
Great workout with really good elevations!!!
Fairly challenging, especially on a hot day. Varied scenery throughout to keep you stimulated. Rarely boring, except a few sections towards the end. Plenty of white trillium in mid May.

Hiked 19.8km through this wonderful park. Lots of elevation especially if your going North on the Bruce trail from Hockley Rd (South of the Park). Pretty steady today with lots of people out. I’m definitely coming back and I’ll include Hockley Eastern Trail another 18km loop trail which is off 2nd Line EHS.

One of the better hikes on Bruce Trail in this area. Very popular place. Parking lot was half full by 9:00 am and people were parking on the road later. Would probably classify as harder than moderate because of a lot of up and down. Trails close to the parking lot were very busy - Tom East Side and Bruce Portion.

Trails are very well marked and groomed as well with lots of small bridges over streams and marshy areas and also steps on steep portions.

Some great riverside locations and one nicely tucked area with stones to make Inukshuk. 

There were many areas with blooms of white Trillium with sprinkling of purple Trillium. 

Trees varied from groves of evergreens to those of deciduous areas. 

We saw what looked like a mink near the stream at the junction of Bruce and Tom East side trail.

Total kms was more like 15 with elevation gain of close to 500m. 

Would definitely do this one again in summer, fall and winter.
Great exercise with elevation changes and a wonderful nature!
Beautiful trail! Lots to see

3.5 Stars actually, not 3.

Pro's:
- great workout, great elevations
- amazingly marked (wouldn't expect any less from the Bruce trail)
- varied terrain and constant scenery changes (rivers, forests, bridges, marshes)
- easy to social distance

Con's:
- After 12km, there is nothing really out of this world extraordinary. No massive lookout vistas, no waterfalls, etc.
- When the wind blows, you may get wafts of cow dung. lol
it's fucking amazing
Great trail. Well marked. Highly recommended
Amazing!
Excellent
beautiful trail. lots of mixture of woods. lots of hills which is great. A lot of people though and dogs off leash :(
Love this trail, saw trout, salamander and a hawk. We will be back to explore more!
Great trail with a ton of elevation. Brings lots of water if you plan to do all the side trails as well. Free parking in the lot on Hockley Valley Rd. Go early if you want a spot!
Lovely park! Parking is east of the trailhead, and you need to walk on the side of the road to get to the trail. Trails were very muddy, but otherwise a perfect day!
It's a challenging trail with many ups and downs.
Total distance was 15km. Lots of ups and downs, a bit crowded towards midday (April 2021) but overall great trail. Good workout and nice scenery.

I just did the main trail today from Hockley Road to Dunby Road and back again. Took me about 3.5 hours. Conditions were good, not muddy at all. I encountered one person all day but it was super cold and windy so to be expected.
Muddy. Icy. Beautiful - cover girl.
Beautiful and well marked.
Popular trail. Very easy to navigate. Elevation is moderate. Very nice scenery.
Great trail with terrain variety and magical winter landscapes. Icers are highly recommended.
Great scenic and well marked trails. Crampons help with the numerous elevation changes.
Perfect condition, snow,well marked,moderate to hard, so you need gear for up or down the hill
Snowy but great condition! The descents  could be a bit slippery, so wear good shoes, and crampons and/or polls recommended.
Gorgeous, I see why this is many people's favourite trail! Definitely need microspikes this time of year, very hilly which makes for a solid leg workout. Can't wait to return!
One of my favourite hikes. Great trail conditions, some snow and ice but well marked and maintained. Weekdays it’s pretty quiet on the trail. Weekends are busy from 10:00 onwards
Fun trail with small climbs.
Great Hike, moderate & hilly, my fav!

This trail was wonderful! Beautiful sights, lots of little streams, and forest. A lot of different elevations. In the winter, maybe wear spikes. Some spots are a bit slippery. Entrance is the diciest spot haha Loved the trail! Also the trail is very well maintained and marked, we were quite impressed :) would definitely hike again !
Walking conditions were great, packed snow covered the whole trail, hardly needed my spikes!
Amazing winter hike. Went in Jan and crampons are a must. Very quiet hike and amazing views all around
Trail was great. Little icy so cleats/micro-spikes needed for sections. Overall a great trail for exercise as there are a lot of hills.
Great trail for Ontario! Fun and undulating terrain.
Tom East Side Trail, Cam Snell Side Trail, and Bruce Trails Loop
Nice workout trail
Great Trail! Not too many sightseeing spots but very hilly. Great hike for a good workout!

beautiful trail but super duper busy. We started at 8am and by 1030am the trails inside were packed. Its largely packed with large groups which is just too much. it was definitely beautiful and I will definitely be back.
Always a delight.
My new favourite!

Hockley Valley is so beautiful!  Late October is a great time of year to enjoy as there are no crowds.  The trail itself is a nice mix of forests, streams and vistas.  Be prepared for a workout going up and down.
Nice but quite busy. 1st car park was full, we had to look for the 2 nd one.
tough but good. :)

Approx. 3.25 hrs to do the full tri-loop. Perfect conditions over the weekend—no bugs, ground was still fairly hard, and even though the parking lot was full, once you get it, you can go without seeing anyone for an hour! 

Would reco layers over the next few weeks. Inclines will get your heart rate up!
7.6km hike and 9km running. great trail for running.
Great trail with a few challenging inclines and the last 2km was quite muddy.
Great trail. Extremely busy today. Parking lot jammed with cars and so was the road. All hikers were good at stepping aside and keeping their distance.  We saw lots of hikers.

Good up and down. My recording shows 14 plus km. I stayed left and did all three loops.  The Cam Snell starts with a down and up through a set of streams and it’s beautiful. Cedars and flowing water with a.bunch of foot bridges. The three side trails offer a great variety of scenery too. Weather was perfect and the fall colours are almost done.  Highly recommend this one in parts it as a whole.

Very nice trail with changing elevations! Dirt and rocks paths that weave through the forest/meadows and over small streams.  Moderately busy trail but with its vast space, it doesn’t become overcrowded.  Would definitely do the trail again!
Great
Lovely trail. Came at 1 PM ET and managed to find parking. Very well marked and moderately crowded on a Saturday. Truly a good one.
Still one of my favourite long hikes in the area! Fall colours have started.
Great hike. lots of exercise with hills and some flat areas to round it out.

Stunning walk. Loads of variety. Took 4 hours at a good clip with 2 short breaks. This is NOT a walk in the park, however; a fairly high level of fitness is required. Also, make sure to arrive early to snag a parking spot!

Very nice maintained well marked quiet trail. The trail takes you through the forest, valley, river, and stream. Great scenery. Elevation was steep at some point so can be challenging for new hikers. I went during the weekday. Only five cars parked in the parking lot. I only saw maybe 4 ppl throughout my 4 hours there.
Well marked! This was our first new trail of 2020c and it did not disappoint. I would come earlier then 9am, as by the time we got back the parking was full!

Lovely trails all three, starting with the easiest Tom East Side which is just around 5kms, then Isabella  side trail and finally Cam Snell Side trail. All three have different things to offer. With the Isabella providing lots of streams and small bridges for good photo opp as well. I have gone through all the three trails mainly for photography and there are lots. In terms of people you will not cross many as the trails are long and not much crowd.

Park in free BT lot - Park in free BT lot
Hockley Rd, Mono, ON L9W 2Y8
https://maps.app.goo.gl/hx9gAYGt9EnoaPwZ7

Decent trail, some challenging climbs (for a beginner) but not many. good mix of flatter and rockier terrain. River portion is nice. not many nice lookouts or views which I like so that's why I gave it 4 stars.

Great trail offering the beginner to intermediate a good challenge with some climbs. That being said the trail is well maintained and the climbs are made a lot easier with all the steps put in by hard working trail volunteers. A lot of great spots to stop creekside or trail side to enjoy a break.
Awesome trail! Nice views, beautiful forest. Well signed and maintained.

Great trail base, well marked except in a couple of places. I had just upgraded to Pro yesterday, and it really helped us get back on the right trail. Much hillier than I expected, so it was quite a workout for a 64 year old.

Nice trail. Not much traffic, we'll marked. Can combine multiple loops based on time, fitness etc. Some ups and down but no scrambling involved. 

Why not 5 stars - the parking lot is about half a km away and you have to walk on roadside to trailhead.
My buddy and I did it in about 3 hours, it was marked very well! Had some great elevation changes, highly recommend
Excellent. Shady and cool.

Great hike! Would recommend having a big breakfast before heading out on your day of hiking if you're doing the full trail. We did the trail in 4.5 hours with a judicious number of stops for the sights and rest.

This trail system took us about 4 hours as we stopped to check out lots of wildlife (didn't do the cam trail). It had wonderful shade most of the way and a few lovely sunny valleys. Lots of challenging elevation for a great workout. The stream running near the trail was beautiful, but made for A LOT of flies in some areas- bring bugspray.

Hiked this trail on July 12th and it's a great system. The hike has a lot of elevation changes and I was surprised by my lack of fitness within the first hour. We ended up only doing the first two loops and it took 3 hours. There are many interesting features along the hike (streams, rivers, bridges, valley, forest, open field etc.) and I highly recommend this trail.
Completed all three loops in about 4 hours. Lovely trail system! We did lose our direction a couple times, but there are maps to help reorient you.

Great trail! I’m new to toronto and have been trying new hikes just outside the city every weekend. This was the 5th one we’ve tried so far (all similar lengths) and this was our favourite one so far! Note: there is one patch that has a CRAZY amount of mosquitos.. I recommend wearing bug spray and running through that section (it doesn’t last very long)
Awesome.  Decent amount of effort

May 31.2020 (sunny approx 8-12 degrees cel)- arrived around 845AM and there were already approx 12 cars. Did the whole route as shown with side trails and took just under 3 hours. A lot of ups, downs and changing scenery: forest, rivers, bridges, a bit of open field, "stairs", etc. It was a very nice hike and enjoyed the hills. Did pass quite a few people so not a quiet trail by any means (passed 3-4 large hiking groups). Wasn't too muddy even though it rained the 2 days before. Although I used bug spray I was never bothered by any.

Definitely a strenuous and extremely beautiful hike; lots of variety in terrain and the majority has heavy tree cover. Should be labelled as “heavily trafficked” as we arrived at 8:15 am and by the time we left around 11:30 am we’d seen dozens of people. If you want solitude, not the best choice. If you want to feel like you’ve done 100 squats, the best choice.

One of the best hikes close to the city, great combination of hills, meadows, rivers and ponds. A lot of ups and downs and lots of bugs but they are good motivation to keep hustling. Would definitely recommend!
First day on the trails 2020.  Nice to be out of the house.
well kept, even in the winter. cool Bridges and landscapes
Took about 4 hours for the full 13.5 km. Lovely trail in the fall.
My pup n I love this trail. Nice mix of hills, field, tree, streams......We have done the low loop and the middle loop but havent ventured the top loop yet.
Beautiful trail! Well maintained and easy to follow. The landscapes and types of forest change through out. Really enjoyed the creek that runs through the second loop. Very peaceful.

This is one of the best trails I’ve ever been to. Features tall trees which makes the path dense and dark giving it a typical forest feeling. We spotted so many flowers and (delicious) apple trees along our way. The side trails open up to small lakes and the scenery is amazing. I will definitely go back here again when the fall colours are in bloom.
Amazing trail, it took us almost 4 hours to complete it. very good marked trail, very beautiful sceneries!

Went on Aug 4, 2019. This trail was incredible! Weather was great, and the bugs were relatively few and easily tolerable. There's a variety of beautiful terrain. Trail is very clearly marked with blazes. This is definitely  my favorite hike so far within easy driving range of Toronto! I can't imagine how great it must be in the fall.
This was one of the best trails I have walked outside of Algonquin Park. It's extremely hilly if you decide to do all three side trails.

100% covered, trail well blazed. However you must be vigilant to follow carefully the blazes b/c it was easy to get strayed into smaller  trails. Full of bugs in July. The slope is gentle b/c  spread over a long distance. A few spots where the slope gets steep, there are steps.

The direction leads to the parking exactly. Thank you to the trail map author. From the parking, there are signs to lead you to the headtrail 200 meters away.
12km Loop in the park. Very shady. Enough creeks for water for your dog and yourself ( I bring my filter bottle). Free parking.

As others have said, a great, varied hike and well worth the effort. Hiked in early July with the water in the streams a little low. All bridges were easily passable, though some of the trail is becoming a little overgrown. Wildflowers were in full bloom. Bugs were about in places, but the deet free bug spray kept them away (unlike Algonquin!). We will be back in fall.

An excellent hike. Surprisingly not a lot of bugs on this warm sunny day. Ample shade through the forest. Also a good work out as the trail undulates quite a bit through different elevations. Don’t let the partial walk on the road to get from parking to trail mislead you. This is a great nature trail and seems almost untouched in many places. Well worth it.

We’ve been coming to this trail for over a decade and it’s one of our favourites. This loop samples all the diverse parts of the park, with different forests and characters, 20+ bridges, and all very well-maintained to Bruce Trail standards. A sloppy, hilly park cut with beautiful rivers.

Hiked in early February on a mild day after a deep freeze. Trail was a river at many points, and iced over from much use. Waterproof boots & ice cleats were necessary. I managed without cleats but it was dicey and I wouldn’t recommend doing it that way. Wanted to avoid the valley for flood risk but it likely would have been the easier route. 

Would come back to try it again in better weather though.
Amazing. Need chains in the winter to be safe. Slipped a few times on icy spots.
Really great trail that is well-maintained and has a lot of great scenery - will definitely be coming again. Free parking is a plus too!
great loop system - lots of elevation changes and types of terrain.  took us about 3.5 hrs with just a couple short water breaks.
